description: A site's JSON for a goal: calls its route, or, with none yet, walks url (a page that does it) once in the browser and keeps the answering call as the route, so the goal then skips the browser. Search terms in the url query (https://example.com/?q=rust) become inputs; a new value is a new call. A route answers only its own page or call address, varying only at inputs; another item, host or query key is learned afresh, never given another page's data. Network routes go first (how: network; paid as unbrowse_call says, nothing to approve): a fee over the owner's per-fetch max, or over budget_usdc when given: network_skipped; a fee not paid (daily limit, balance): payment_refused, with what the owner can do. Needs clicks or typing: how: browse, page open (in session, if given) with a snapshot: go on in unbrowse_browse; the call your steps send becomes the route. Reply: result (ok, data, retry, ignored_inputs), how (called|network|learned|browse), route.also_sends (non-read steps before the answer, a POST: read before calling again), optional inputs (filter, sort, next page) with options; more may appear as a learned route tries its page's controls in the background. result.more: inputs for a list's next page; none: it ended. Another page of the kind: the same call with its url, answered in a fraction of a second; many: one call with pages. Check data against your goal: you can tell what the node can't. Wrong (empty, another thing, suggestions, wrong tab): unbrowse_judge, then ask again.

ask.description: From a still_working reply: collects the answer, waiting up to wait_ms again. Kept 5 min after the work ends. Alone: it holds the rest.

browser.description: auto (default): when needed, fetched if missing and the owner allows; if_present: only one present; never: routes, network routes, plain requests only. Missing: error and outcome browser_missing, saying what and how to get it; ruled out: that error, outcome browser_declined, declined: true, nothing to install, next: the call with browser auto.

budget_usdc.description: USDC this task pays at most to fetch one network route (e.g. 0.01); a fee over it is passed over (network_skipped). Only lowers the owner's max.

fields.description: Extra paths from result.fields.more (items[].rating; a list or object brings all of it), or ["*"]. Default: the goal's fields and each record's name. Ask only for what you need.

goal.description: Plain words; the same ones find the same route. Needed unless ask.

inputs.description: By route.inputs names; win over the url's.

pages.description: Instead of url, max 100 (objects or url strings), side by side; a page's goal and inputs win. Reply how: pages: each page's how, ms, data or error, in order; fields once per route. A site's first page goes first; its route answers the rest. A how: browse page isn't opened: ask it alone. Past wait_ms (40 s unsaid), pages still learning are how: working, in pending. The batch's ask (in next) collects it all; each page's own ask, that page; unbrowse_do of that page alone joins its walk.

wait_ms.description: ms; default 45000, max 300000. Then, still working (learning, waiting for the site's browser): outcome still_working with ask and next; work goes on.

name: unbrowse_do
title: Connect to a site
